blocks.content: The President may be removed from office for violation of the Constitution by impeachment under Article 61.

rows: Proportional Representation by single transferable vote
2/3rd majority of the total membership of each House

items: The phrase 'violation of the Constitution' is NOT defined anywhere in the Constitution of India.
Impeachment requires a majority of 2/3rd of the TOTAL membership of the House (not present and voting), which is unique in Indian Constitutional law.
Nominated members of either House of Parliament CAN participate in the impeachment process, despite not being eligible to vote in the Presidential election.
Elected members of State Legislative Assemblies and UTs DO NOT participate in the impeachment process, despite being part of the Electoral College during elections.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The President of India can be removed from office before the expiry of term through the process of impeachment under Article 61.
The sole ground for impeachment specified in the Constitution is 'violation of the Constitution'.
An impeachment motion can be initiated in either House of Parliament (Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha).
The resolution requires a special majority of two-thirds of the total membership of both Houses to pass.
The impeachment process is a quasi-judicial procedure in Parliament where the President has the right to appear and be represented.
